title: My WoW bot opens its own repair tickets. 110 so far, only 4 are proven fixed
author: IndiBestEngineer
selftext:
I'm building a bot that plays World of Warcraft by itself. An addon inside the game writes its state (position, target, health, quests, bags), the bot reads that, and a model only plans: next goal, next pull. No screenshots in the loop.

When it gets stuck, the loop opens a repair ticket, a Claude Code session writes a fix, and a judge decides later whether the fix worked. The judge doesn't count hours, it counts chances: fights, deaths, time the bot was actually driving. If the old symptom had enough chances to come back and didn't, the verdict is "helped". Too few chances and it's "not verified", never "fixed".

Numbers after a few weeks: 110 tickets. 4 helped, 21 not verified, 22 still waiting in game for enough chances. Most of the "not verified" are rare symptoms. If I counted those as wins, the loop would look about 6 times better than it is.

The bug that taught me this: one night the bot spent 8 hours as a ghost walking to its own corpse, 11,366 times "reached, 2 yards". Every counter said it was moving. Now I check progress, not activity.

How do you verify a fix for something that only happens once a night?
